extracted.intended_audience: general public, potential partners/donors, collaborators and journalists interested in nonprofit investigative reporting on inequality
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational mission, values and standards that guide a nonprofit investigative newsroom focused on inequality; describes topical focus, journalistic practices, collaboration and measures of impact. Useful for understanding how to produce or assess Public Integrity’s reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on inequality
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Integrity is focusing its investigative reporting on inequality, a problem ingrained in the culture and economy of the U.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization directs reporting resources to systems and circumstances that contribute to inequality rather than treating inequality as an incidental topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission: hold powerful interests accountable and equip the public
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Integrity seeks to counter the corrosive effects of inequality by holding powerful interests accountable and equipping the public with knowledge to drive change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting should be oriented toward producing information that enables public action and accountability rather than purely descriptive coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence, nonpartisanship and nonprofit status
rubrics_metrics.description: We are an independent, nonpartisan and nonprofit news organization dedicated to investigating systems and circumstances that contribute to inequality in our country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial decisions are framed by institutional independence; the organization explicitly separates itself from partisan advocacy and relies on a nonprofit funding model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject-matter expertise domains
rubrics_metrics.description: Reporters excel at investigating the systems and circumstances that contribute to inequality in labor, housing, health care, education and access to democracy, and examine disparities in environmental and criminal justice, transportation, technology and access to financial tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coverage priorities include the listed domains; investigative teams are expected to develop domain expertise to expose structural drivers of inequity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth
rubrics_metrics.description: We strive to provide a definitive look at the issues we tackle, examining the context and history of inequitable systems and evaluating solutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stories should go beyond surface reporting to include historical context, systemic analysis and assessment of potential solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration
rubrics_metrics.description: We broaden the reach of our investigations by partnering with national and local news organizations, especially in underserved communities, and work with trusted local influencers so more people have access to our work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partnerships with other newsrooms and community influencers are a core tactic to increase reach and local impact; collaboration is prioritized particularly where local trust and distribution matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equitable access and funding model
rubrics_metrics.description: We believe access to information is key to equity. Our journalism is free to all. Our work is supported by philanthropy, sponsorships and individual donations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content should remain freely accessible; funding sources (philanthropy, sponsorships, donations) are used rather than paywalls or advertising that could restrict access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tenacity / resilience against external pressure
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether it’s online harassment, trolling of our journalists or threat of lawsuits aimed at silencing our investigations, we do not bow down to external pressure and will continue to expose inequities that have harmed marginalized communities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The newsroom commits to persisting with investigations despite harassment, legal threats or other attempts to intimidate; risk and legal preparation are implied practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture of belonging, diversity and transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: We acknowledge journalism’s role in upholding inequality and mainstream media’s historical failure to provide fair and accurate coverage about marginalized communities. We pursue diverse voices on our staff and in our stories and strive for greater transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hiring, sourcing and editorial choices should prioritize diverse perspectives and transparent practices that address past failures in coverage of marginalized groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurable impact: law and policy changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Integrity confronts inequality through investigative journalism that has led to hundreds of law and policy changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One measure of success for investigations is demonstrable policy or legislative change resulting from reporting; journalists should document and track such outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurable impact: prompting government and institutional action
rubrics_metrics.description: The organization has forced federal and state governments to release information, sparked criminal investigations, and prompted executive actions (for example, agency proposals and administration protections) following its investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Impact includes concrete government responses such as information disclosure, investigations, administrative proposals or new protections; reporting should aim to surface evidence that compels such responses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition and awards as impact indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Integrity’s work has been recognized with prizes and nominations including the Pulitzer Prize, Peabody nomination, Edward R. Murrow Award, and others.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External recognition and journalism awards are cited as validation and indicators of the quality and influence of investigative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsroom composition and diversity metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Our newsroom includes award-winning reporters, editors and data journalists from diverse backgrounds; Public Integrity went from 85% white and majority men in 2016 to now majority journalists of color and women. Across the organization, at least 10% of our team identify as LGBTQI+, and at least 10% identify as having some kind of disability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization tracks and reports demographic composition as part of its commitment to diversity; staffing composition is both a value and a metric for internal progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: No advertising and free readership
rubrics_metrics.description: The Center for Public Integrity is a nonprofit investigative news organization focused on inequality in the U.S. We do not accept advertising or charge people to read our work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial independence is linked to the choice not to accept advertising and to keep content freely available; this is presented as a policy affecting both funding and distribution.
